ESP.note: 70 GEN-mapped projects (2nd only to USA) and dozens of re-inhabited abandoned villages; suelo rústico rules make new rural dwellings hard, so buying an old aldea is the usual route.

CHE.note: Strong cooperative-housing culture, but strict zoning outside building zones and very high land prices; homeschooling rules vary by canton.

AUS.note: Permaculture's birthplace; NSW/Qld 'multiple occupancy' and community-title zoning enabled Crystal Waters and Northern Rivers communities; council approval still needed.

PRT.note: Europe's fastest-growing ecovillage scene (Alentejo/Centro); cheap rural land but RAN/REN farmland & reserve zoning limit new builds, so buy land with ruins or existing licences.

NZL.note: Established network of 1970s-90s communities; Building Act consents required but off-grid, composting toilets and small dwellings are workable; homeschool needs MoE exemption.

ITA.note: RIVE network plus Damanhur precedent; thousands of depopulated borghi to restore; istruzione parentale legal with annual exam, but new rural construction is tightly controlled.

JPN.note: Old communal precedents (Atarashiki-mura 1918, Yamagishi) and millions of empty akiya; farmland law restricts building on agricultural land and foreigners face rural integration hurdles.

DEU.note: Densest mature community scene in Europe (eurotopia, Kommuja, GEN-D); but homeschooling is banned and Außenbereich (§35 BauGB) bars new rural settlements, so groups buy estates.

AUT.note: Active GEN/community network; home education legal with annual exams (tightened 2021); Grünland zoning makes new rural dwellings difficult.

FRA.note: Cooperative Oasis has recorded 1,600+ eco-lieux projects; ALUR law recognises 'habitat leger' (yurts/tiny homes) but home education now needs prior authorisation (2022).

DNK.note: ~30 ecovillages in LØS plus hundreds of bofællesskaber cohousing groups; homeschooling legal; rural zoning (landzone) strict but ecovillages get local-plan approval.

TWN.note: Experimental Education Act (2014) gives strong legal room for alternative/community schools; farmland-house rules and high land prices restrict new settlements.

NLD.note: Ecodorpen network of ~30 initiatives, often municipal plots; extremely tight spatial planning and homeschooling only via narrow exemptions.

GBR.note: Findhorn precedent and ~170 established communities (Diggers & Dreamers); home education fully legal; Wales' One Planet Development policy is the only easy route to rural self-build.

NOR.note: Small scene centred on Hurdal; homeschooling legal under municipal supervision; concession and agricultural land rules limit buying and building rural plots.

USA.note: Largest ecosystem: FIC directory ~1,600 listings, 114 GEN-mapped; homeschooling legal everywhere; many rural counties have no building codes, though zoning varies hugely.

KOR.note: Strong maeul (village) community-building movement and alternative schools; homeschooling legally grey but tolerated; farmland and building permits restrictive.

CAN.note: Mature scene, esp. BC & Quebec; homeschooling legal in all provinces; rural zoning varies - BC's Agricultural Land Reserve limits extra dwellings.

BEL.note: Growing habitat groupe/cohousing movement; home education is a constitutional right (with exams); dense planning limits rural self-build.

HKG.note: Essentially no land for a new community; homeschooling handled case-by-case by the Education Bureau.

ISL.note: Sólheimar (1930) is a world-class precedent; geothermal energy abundant; homeschooling requires a certified teacher.

SWE.note: Long ekoby tradition and allemansrätt culture; cheap rural land, but homeschooling effectively banned since 2011 - a community would need its own approved friskola.

GRC.note: Young but growing permaculture/ecovillage scene; cheap rural land, permissive in practice; homeschooling illegal.

ISR.note: ~270 kibbutzim (126,000 people, 2010) are the world's largest intentional-community precedent; but 93% state land and tight planning make new settlements political.

FIN.note: Small scene; home education legal with municipal progress checks; abundant cheap forest land, building permits needed but rural rules relatively flexible.

LUX.note: Tiny scene and very expensive land; homeschooling legal with notification.

IRL.note: Cloughjordan is Ireland's flagship; a dozen-plus Camphill communities; home education is a constitutional right; one-off rural housing faces planning scrutiny.

SMR.note: Microstate with no known communities and very limited land.

SYC.note: No known communities; land scarce and foreign land purchases need government sanction.

HRV.note: Small emerging scene (Istria, Slavonia) with cheap abandoned farmsteads; homeschooling illegal.

POL.note: Few established ecovillages but cheap rural land; home education legal (54,836 children, 2024); farmland purchase restricted to farmers by 2016 law.

AND.note: No known communities; tiny, mountainous and expensive.

CZE.note: New GEN Czechoslovakia network (2024); individual home education legal at primary level; cheap rural property in border regions.

CYP.note: A handful of eco-tourism villages; homeschooling illegal; divided island complicates land titles.

SVN.note: Small permaculture scene; home education legal with annual exams; agricultural land building limits.

BRB.note: No known communities; small island, high land costs.

MUS.note: One GEN-listed initiative; land expensive and foreign purchase limited to approved schemes.

SGP.note: Urban farm community only; no land for a settlement; homeschool needs MOE exemption.

BHS.note: No established communities; island land costly; hurricane building codes.

CRI.note: ~30 GEN-mapped projects and a big regenerative/expat scene; easy foreign land ownership; homeschooling not legal for citizens (exam-based 'educación abierta' is the workaround).

ROU.note: Cheap land and depopulating villages in Transylvania; permissive rural building; homeschooling only for special circumstances.

URY.note: Small scene; stable, easy for foreigners to buy land; home education confirmed legal by 2020 amendment.

TTO.note: One known spiritual community; homeschooling legal.

ARG.note: Gaia (1992) is a regional pioneer and GEN training hub; cheap land; home education needs provincial permission; border security zones restrict foreign buyers.

BGR.note: Cheap village houses attract a growing foreign eco-scene; permissive rural building; homeschooling restricted to special cases.

EST.note: Active Estonian community network and Gaia education; home education legal under school supervision; plentiful forest land.

SVK.note: A few rural ecovillage projects; individual education legal for ages 6-15; low land prices.

MYS.note: Small scene; foreigners face minimum-price rules for land; homeschooling allowed with Education Ministry exemption.

CHL.note: Solid scene incl. Peñalolén (1980s) and many parcelas de agrado projects; homeschool legal via exámenes libres; DL 3516 rural-parcel subdivisions face tightening rules.

ARE.note: No intentional communities; Masdar is a state eco-city; homeschooling legal for expats.

MLT.note: No known communities; very little rural land; homeschooling illegal.

BRA.note: Large ecovila movement (CASA Brasil, IPEC); cheap land but foreign rural ownership capped; homeschooling unregulated after 2018 Supreme Court ruling.

MDV.note: No known communities; land leased from state.

MEX.note: GEN co-founder Huehuecoyotl (Tepoztlán) and 44 GEN-mapped sites; self-build widely tolerated; avoid ejido land titles and foreign 'restricted zone' coastline.

ECU.note: Constitution grants Rights of Nature; Vilcabamba/Andes expat-eco cluster; home education (educación en casa) is regulated by the Education Ministry.

BTN.note: Gross National Happiness ethos, but foreigners cannot own land and entry is tightly controlled.

CUB.note: Strong state-backed urban agroecology/permaculture, but private land and independent schooling are not possible.

THA.note: Thriving natural-building/permaculture scene around Chiang Mai and Asoke Buddhist communities; foreigners cannot own land (leases/Thai partners).

LTU.note: Small scene; home education legal under school supervision.

GEO.note: Cheap land and liberal building practice attract new projects; foreigners restricted from buying farmland; homeschooling not legally provided.

TUR.note: Active permaculture/eco-farm network (TaTuTa); homeschooling illegal; agricultural land building and foreign ownership rules restrictive.

PER.note: Sacred Valley/Andes spiritual-eco cluster; informal rural building common; home education legal with Ministry registration.

HUN.note: Krishna Valley and Gyűrűfű are long-running precedents; cheap rural land; homeschooling effectively curtailed since 2019; foreigners limited on farmland.

TON.note: Land cannot be sold to foreigners (lease only).

WSM.note: Most land is customary and inalienable; leases only.

ARM.note: A couple of small projects; homeschooling illegal; cheap land.

SAU.note: No intentional communities; strict social and land controls.

DMA.note: One GEN-listed project; volcanic 'nature island' with cheap land.

LVA.note: Small rural eco-homestead scene; home education legal under school supervision.

IND.note: Auroville (1968) is the template; strong ashram/Gandhian precedent; NIOS open schooling legal; foreigners cannot buy farmland - needs Indian trust/society ownership.

PAN.note: Expat-friendly land purchase; small eco-scene; homeschooling legal status unclear.

COL.note: 31 GEN-mapped sites, CASA Colombia network and Gaviotas (1971) precedent; home education regulated with validation exams; check security and land-restitution history.

CHN.note: Rural-revitalisation eco-villages exist but land is collectively owned; foreigners cannot buy land and homeschooling is illegal.

VNM.note: Only eco-tourism projects; all land state-owned, foreigners cannot hold rural land.

LKA.note: Sarvodaya movement active in ~15,000 villages (2006) - a huge village-self-help precedent; foreigners restricted from freehold land.

SEN.note: Government ecovillage agency (ANEV, 2008) and GENSEN network - one of the few states that promotes ecovillages officially; land via commune allocation.

ZAF.note: Active ecovillage/permaculture scene in Western Cape; home education legal with provincial registration; SANS 10400 building rules apply, rural approval possible.

IDN.note: Bali's eco/Green School scene; homeschooling (sekolah rumah) legal; foreigners can only lease land (Hak Pakai/PMA company).

BOL.note: Small scene; Pachamama law recognises Rights of Mother Earth; cheap land.

RUS.note: ~5-6 Anastasia 'kin domain' settlements per region (12,000 settlers, 2016); family education legal; cheap land, but political and sanctions risk for foreigners.

DOM.note: Few projects; easy foreign land purchase.

PRY.note: Mennonite colonies (since 1927) show communal settlement works; cheap land, easy residency; few ecovillages.

TZA.note: All land is state; foreigners only via TIC investment leases.

GTM.note: Lake Atitlán permaculture scene; homeschooling illegal per Wikipedia table.

PHL.note: Homeschooling formally recognised by DepEd; foreigners cannot own land (60/40 rule).

GHA.note: 16 GEN-mapped projects, GEN Africa activity; customary land via chiefs; foreigners get 50-year leases.

BLZ.note: Easy freehold purchase for foreigners; permissive rural building.

FJI.note: Mostly iTaukei customary land; leases only.

NPL.note: 17 GEN-mapped projects and strong permaculture NGO network; foreigners cannot own land.

KEN.note: Active permaculture/GEN Africa scene; foreigners limited to 99-year leaseholds; homeschooling status contested.

MDA.note: Cheap land and permissive building; foreigners cannot buy farmland.

JOR.note: Greening the Desert permaculture demo site; arid, water-scarce.

ALB.note: No established communities yet; cheap coastal/hill land; homeschooling legal with regulation (2012).

NIC.note: Ometepe island eco-scene; political risk since 2018.

UKR.note: Pre-war GEN Ukraine & Anastasia-style settlements; family education legal; war makes new projects unrealistic.

BWA.note: No known communities; homeschooling legal; tribal land allocations.

RWA.note: Strict planning (imidugudu villagisation, thatch bans); stable governance.

TUV.note: Atoll nation; no land for outsiders.

SRB.note: Cheap abandoned villages; homeschooling only for health reasons per Wikipedia table.

ETH.note: All land is state-owned; leases only; civil-conflict risk.

FSM.note: No known communities; foreigners cannot own land.

MAR.note: Growing permaculture/eco-lodge scene; foreigners cannot buy agricultural land.

TLS.note: No known communities; foreigners cannot own land.

HND.note: One listed project; high crime risk.

MNG.note: No ecovillages found; nomadic land-use culture; land leasing possible.

IRN.note: One ecovillage near Qazvin; strong state control.

KIR.note: Atoll nation; no land for outsiders.

ZMB.note: Permaculture networks; customary land via chiefs.

LAO.note: No known communities; foreigners cannot own land.

BLR.note: A few rural eco-homesteads; authoritarian state, homeschooling illegal.

UGA.note: 12 GEN-mapped projects incl. SINA youth communities; mailo/customary land; foreigners only lease.

SWZ.note: Swazi Nation Land allocated by chiefs.

ZWE.note: Kufunda and Chikukwa are respected African permaculture precedents; land tenure insecure for outsiders.

MWI.note: Strong permaculture NGOs (e.g., Kusamala); customary land.

EGY.note: Sekem (1977) is a celebrated biodynamic desert-reclamation community; building on Nile farmland is banned, desert land via state allocation.

BFA.note: Strong agroecology roots (zai pits, Pierre Rabhi's work); severe insecurity since 2016.

NGA.note: Little ecovillage activity; insecurity in many states.

CMR.note: Ndanifor is a regional permaculture hub; Anglophone-region conflict risk.

COD.note: 11 GEN-listed projects; very insecure in the east.

_sources.GEN map: Global Ecovillage Network directory (ecovillage.org/map), 1,337 community listings scraped Oct 2026; 1,098 with coordinates reverse-geocoded to countries with Natural Earth 1:50m boundaries. Per-country GEN counts are a floor for ecoCount.
_sources.FIC: Foundation for Intentional Community directory (ic.org/directory) - 1,610 listings total.

national networks.GBR: Diggers & Dreamers 13th ed.: 84+85 existing, 10+17 developing communities

_sources.homeschool: Wikipedia 'Homeschooling international status and statistics' (country tables + per-country sections, incl. HSLDA-cited entries); 'unclear' where no source found. Ecuador from author knowledge.
_sources.pins: ecovillages.json coordinates from Wikipedia/Wikidata (P625), GEN map markers, OpenStreetMap Nominatim, Japan GSI geocoder; founding year/population from Wikipedia/Wikidata, GEN listings (self-reported 'Founding year'/'Total') or the community's own site.
_sources.other: Land-ownership, zoning and legal notes from author knowledge of national law (not re-verified this session; web search quota was exhausted).

_method.eco: 0-100 judgement score of the existing ecovillage/intentional-community ecosystem: density of GEN-mapped projects, national networks and directories, long-lived precedent communities (10+ yrs), permaculture/regenerative culture. Anchors: USA 100, Germany 98, Portugal/Spain/France 92.
_method.ecoCount: Order-of-magnitude count of known ecovillages + intentional communities (max of GEN map count and national directory/network estimates; cohousing included only where noted).
_method.examples: Up to 4 notable existing communities; names from GEN listings, Wikipedia or national networks.
_method.homeschool: legal = permitted with minimal oversight; regulated = permitted with registration/exams/exemption; restricted = only narrow exceptions or prior authorisation; banned = illegal; unclear = no clear legal provision or source.
_method.offgrid: 0-100 judgement of how permissive building/zoning/utility rules are for rural self-build, natural building, composting toilets, off-grid utilities and multiple dwellings (de-facto enforcement considered). Does not score land-ownership limits for foreigners (noted in 'note').
_method.est: true = thin data (fewer than 5 GEN-mapped projects and no national directory figure), values largely expert-estimated; false = eco/ecoCount anchored on counted directory data.
